description: Price-discovery sources for water treatment chemical procurement, derived from full read of all 46 EPA Water Treatment Chemical Supply Chain Profiles. Each source notes coverage, access, and the chemicals it informs. Used by the Risk Monitor and Bid Evaluator to ground price-adjusted scoring in defensible public data.

tiers.tier_1_government_free: First-call sources for any procurement decision. Free, authoritative, no licensing risk.
tiers.tier_2_industry_free: Trade associations and producer disclosures. Free but require parsing.
tiers.tier_3_paid_commercial: Subscription required. Add when defensibility or recency demands it.

sources.name: USITC DataWeb
sources.implied_unit_price: import_value_usd / import_volume_kg gives landed-unit-price proxy by HTS x partner
sources.notes: Foundation source — every chemical has trade data here. Limitation: HTS codes are often broader than the chemical (e.g., 2828.90 lumps NaOCl/Ca(OCl)2/NaClO2).

sources.name: USITC Harmonized Tariff Schedule Search
sources.notes: Critical for landed-cost. China Section 301 (25%) is universal across this corpus. Watch antidumping cliffs: Calcium Hypochlorite from China +65.85% CVD; Potassium Permanganate from China +128.94% AD.

sources.name: WITS — World Integrated Trade Solution
sources.notes: Use to identify global price arbitrage and substitute-source countries when primary import partner becomes constrained.

sources.name: EPA TSCA Chemical Data Reporting
sources.notes: Heavy CBI redaction limits utility for organics (citric acid, acrylamide, DADMAC, calcium hypochlorite). Mineral commodities go to USGS instead.

sources.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries
sources.notes: Best free pricing source for mined inputs. Annual unit values ($/ton) are usable directly as procurement benchmarks.

sources.name: USGS Minerals Yearbook
sources.covers_chemicals: same as MCS but with deeper history and breakdowns
sources.notes: Use when MCS is too summary; cited heavily in EPA profiles for bauxite, lime, soda ash, salt, sulfur, manganese, zinc.

sources.name: USITC Investigation Publications
sources.notes: Antidumping reports contain rare disclosed transaction prices and producer capacity figures.

sources.name: NSF International — NSF/ANSI Standard 60 Certified Suppliers
sources.notes: The single most important supplier-pool depth signal. NSF60-certified count varies dramatically (PAC: 140, sodium hydroxide: 224, ferrous sulfate: 5, calcium hypochlorite: 14). Use as the gating criterion for any drinking-water RFP supplier shortlist.

sources.name: EPA Chemical Suppliers and Manufacturers Locator Tool
sources.notes: Companion to NSF60. Geographic distance to nearest supplier is a freight-cost proxy and resilience signal.

sources.name: Federal Register — Antidumping & Countervailing Duty Orders
sources.notes: Watch for new orders that change landed-cost overnight. Set alerts on chemical-specific docket numbers.

sources.name: EIA — Henry Hub Natural Gas Spot Price
sources.notes: Not cited in EPA profiles but is THE upstream driver for ammonia. ~75-80% of global ammonia is steam-methane reformed; gas is ~70% of variable cost.

sources.name: EIA — WTI Crude and Refinery Throughput
sources.notes: Refinery utilization is inverse to sulfur availability — when refineries idle, sulfur tightens.

sources.name: BLS Producer Price Index — Industrial Chemicals
sources.notes: Not cited in EPA profiles but standard for spot-price escalation and contract index clauses. Use as price-adjustment index in long-term RFP boilerplate.

sources.name: The Chlorine Institute — Production & Shipment Reports, Pamphlets
sources.access: Most pamphlets free; quarterly production data subscription/member
sources.notes: The only granular source for chlorine production figures (10,000 M kg in 2019). Critical for chlor-alkali family pricing.

sources.name: AWWA B-Series Water Treatment Chemical Standards
sources.notes: Spec compliance gate. RFP technical specs should reference these directly.

sources.name: ICIS (Independent Commodity Intelligence Services)
sources.notes: Cited in HCl profile (Bowen 2020). Industry-standard for forward-curve pricing.

sources.name: S&P Global Commodity Insights (formerly Platts)
sources.notes: Standard for fertilizer-overlap chemicals where ag pricing dominates.

sources.name: Argus Media
sources.notes: Strong on fertilizer chain — useful for phosphate/sulfur derivatives.

sources.name: Chemical Market Analytics (formerly IHS Markit chemical)
sources.notes: Cited in NaOH profile (Kreuz 2022). Best forward-looking supply-demand model for chlor-alkali.

sources.name: Chemical & Engineering News (C&EN)
sources.notes: Cited multiple times (Tullo 2021 Gulf Coast force majeure; Boerner 2019 ammonia energy; McCoy 2008 acid pricing).

sources.name: World Bank Commodity Markets Outlook (Pink Sheet)
sources.notes: Cited via Baffes & Koh 2022 — flagged 178% potash price increase Apr 2021–Apr 2022.

sources.name: gasworld trade publication
sources.access: Free articles, paid subscription for premium

sources.name: NOAA Storm Prediction & Hurricane Tracking
sources.notes: Winter Storm Uri (Feb 2021) caused 28% chlor-alkali capacity loss. Hurricane Ida (Aug 2021) idled Gulf Coast acrylonitrile/allyl chloride. Use NOAA APIs in Risk Monitor as a leading indicator.

sources.name: Producer Annual Reports & 10-K filings
sources.access: Free via SEC EDGAR for public producers
sources.notes: 10-K MD&A sections often include explicit pricing trend commentary.

sources.name: FTC Antitrust Decisions and Consent Orders
sources.notes: Reveal hard truths about merchant vs. captive splits and geographic shipping economics (e.g., 250-300 mile economic truck radius for sodium hypochlorite).

mined_minerals.rationale: USGS publishes named-producer unit values for free; commodity minerals are price-discovered globally.

chlor_alkali_family.rationale: Co-production stoichiometry binds prices; chlorine demand is fundamentally captive (PVC); Gulf Coast weather risk dominates.

petrochem_polymers.rationale: Acrylonitrile and allyl chloride are propylene derivatives; SNF Holding dominates supply; Gulf Coast force majeure recurrent.

ammonia_chain.rationale: Henry Hub gas drives 70% of variable cost. Geopolitical exposure (Russia, Trinidad) tracked through trade flows.

phosphate_chain.rationale: ~95% of phosphate rock is captive for fertilizer; non-fertilizer water-grade derivatives ride fertilizer cycle. Antidumping cases on Chinese phosphates create cliffs.

industrial_gases.rationale: Local pipeline / cylinder / cryo-trailer distribution dominates; international trade is minimal; Big 4 (Linde, Air Liquide/Praxair, Air Products, Matheson) set merchant prices.

specialty_organics.rationale: Heavily import-dependent (China dominates global supply); CBI hides domestic production figures.
